requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 communicate only through node1 via static addressing on their private-network interfaces (dhcp=false), with routes via node1
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook run (cmd-aa1e7895a6514017) applied static IPs 10.10.10.2/24 on node2 and 10.10.20.2/24 on node3 via nmcli, changed=3 on each. Post-run ip addr/ip route (cmd-21ef2b6292234a6f, cmd-6216f21241584368) confirm the static addresses and cross-subnet routes via node1's gateway IPs (10.10.10.1 / 10.10.20.1).

requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured as the router with static IPs on eth1 (facing node2) and eth2 (facing node3)
requirements.summary: Playbook task 'Push VyOS configuration' returned changed:[node1]; config.boot and live ip addr on node1 (cmd-856d7ad7e5d342b5, cmd-46333873aadb4d5f) show eth1=10.10.10.1/24 and eth2=10.10.20.1/24 persisted.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node2 toward node3 is limited to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: tc qdisc on node1's eth2 (cmd-46333873aadb4d5f) shows an htb root qdisc from the VyOS qos shaper policy (bandwidth 1mbit). iperf3 from node2 to node3 (cmd-5c1b7c0b630f468f) settled at ~1.04 Mbit/s sender / 953 Kbit/s receiver, matching the configured cap.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node3 toward node2 is left unrestricted
requirements.summary: tc qdisc on node1's eth1 (facing node2) shows only plain fq_codel, no shaping class (cmd-46333873aadb4d5f). iperf3 from node3 to node2 (cmd-ecc6728a7d6f4cff) reached ~1.5-2 Gbit/s with zero retransmits, confirming no cap in the reverse direction.

requirements.requirement: Implemented using Ansible, run from the designated control node (node4)
requirements.summary: All configuration (nmcli static IP/routes on node2/node3, VyOS interface+QoS config on node1) was applied through an ansible-playbook run executed on node4 (cmd-aa1e7895a6514017), which environment.toml designates as control_node. A subsequent clean re-run (cmd-4ff12b3a38674dd6) confirms idempotency.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) Provider-wide node-restart evidence for all four managed nodes: baseline, reboot, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: For each of node1-node4, evidence shows a pre-reboot boot_id/health baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, connection timeouts consistent with the outage, a new distinct boot_id post-reboot, and directly observed recovery of relevant state: node1's interface addresses and htb shaper config (cmd-90cc2ca86a8d4f72), node2/node3's static IP, route, and successful cross-node ping (cmd-8df508a9f9e74e95, cmd-94b39ed0a70f4b65), and node4's intact ansible project plus a successful post-reboot playbook re-run (cmd-4ff12b3a38674dd6) after fixing a VyOS SSH-key reconciler issue. This aligns with the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots, which independently confirm all four boot IDs changed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly and concretely verified: node2 and node3 received static addressing and routes via node1, node1 was configured as router with static eth1/eth2 addresses, an HTB shaper limits node2->node3 traffic to ~1 Mbit/s (confirmed via tc qdisc and iperf3 measuring ~1.04 Mbit/s), and reverse traffic node3->node2 remains unrestricted (confirmed via tc qdisc and iperf3 measuring ~1.5-2 Gbit/s). The entire configuration was applied idempotently via an Ansible playbook run from control node4. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity transitions and recovered functional state, including a node1-specific complication (VyOS wiping a manually-added SSH key on reboot) that was correctly diagnosed and fixed with a persistent config-based key entry, after which the playbook re-ran successfully.
limitations: No final confirmation was captured that the cluster SSH key added to node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (cmd-2993a5d548e0444e) was removed; its practical risk appears low since the root account is locked and pubkey root login failed, but cleanup was not evidenced.

The single successful node2->node3 iperf3 run and single node3->node2 iperf3 run constitute the primary throughput evidence; no repeated trials were captured to rule out transient variance, though the observed numbers align tightly with the configured 1mbit cap and are far outside normal variance for the unrestricted direction.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were bounded, purposeful, and reverted where temporary (iperf3 firewalld port openings on node2/node3 were opened and closed in cmd-e61d159378e84e67/cmd-8335bdf76bde4394/cmd-2131d4355598494c; a VyOS eth1 description used to validate the config-commit mechanism was set in cmd-c351ced245c04291/cmd-b987facacd414fd3 and cleanly removed in cmd-3f67045823b54fb3/cmd-f8909b03d86741c0). However, two mutations lack a clear final resolution: (1) cmd-2993a5d548e0444e added the cluster SSH private key's public counterpart to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys on the VyOS router node1 as a troubleshooting workaround for privilege escalation; this was superseded by the become=sudo/vyos-user approach used in the final inventory and was never shown to be removed, leaving unused root-level SSH key material on the router (lower risk since root's password is locked per cmd-60fcc17c802c4397, and pubkey root login was observed failing in cmd-89e0733483eb47af, but the credential file itself was not confirmed cleaned up). (2) cmd-5f3529b794624cac manually appended the cluster key directly into /home/vyos/.ssh/authorized_keys, a file VyOS auto-regenerates; this was implicitly wiped by the system's login reconciler across the node1 reboot and correctly replaced with a persistent `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config entry (cmd-b94e012132954324), so no residue remained from this specific action. Neither mutation was destructive or broad, and the core shaping solution itself was clean, idempotent, and left no dangling test artifacts.
